findings.claim: Claim under test: 'Only an exhausted list yields no handle, so withdrawing the preferred copy falls through to the next EQUIVALENT copy (same document id + content hash, no download)' (B02 step description / b-design B02 segment 3 / L03 acceptance 'all copies unusable -> unavailable, do not take another revision').
findings.evidence: Temp harness probe_scenarios.py wrong_bytes, run against BOTH trees (PYTHONPATH=<pre-b02 worktree c986c7a>/src and PYTHONPATH=<company-wiki cab1fd6>/src); fixture: 3 byte-identical copies of one annual report (companies p10 / Dropbox p30 / future_lake p40), then p10 AND p40 deleted and the surviving p30 file rewritten with different bytes (catalog rows/manifest still claim the original hash). document_claimed_sha256=92972bd8...d14dd byte_size=28; served copy actual sha256=1e3e31ffc34ebf7b... size=34. PRE-B02  -> {"status": "missing", "download_required": true, "match_count": 0, "full_trace": ["entity_gate_rejected: 0", "2025: placeholder_no_handle"]}. POST-B02 -> {"status": "reused_exact", "download_required": false, "match_count": 1, "canonical_path": ".../Dropbox/Stock/2025.pdf", "content_sha256": "92972bd8...d14dd" (the CLAIMED hash, not the bytes'), "served_bytes_are_the_requested_version": false, "full_trace": ["2025: unverified_bytes", "2025: candidate <loc1>:not_readable", "2025: candidate <loc2>:size_mismatch:34!=28", "2025: candidate <loc3>:not_readable", "2025: matched"]}.
findings.impact: The read path can now hand out (and report as verified-reusable, download_required=false) a copy whose bytes are provably NOT the requested version - the exact fail-closed case pre-B02 refused (MISSING -> download). This is not merely 'unverified': the size screen AND the full-file digest both failed. It contradicts the run's own L03 acceptance line in test-acceptance-map.md ('all copies unusable -> unavailable, do not take another revision') and the equivalence wording of the claim. The only covering deviation, S-10, is registered as NOT approved (owner-scope-decisions-2026-09-12.md section 9: 'pending owner', 'does not consider itself approved'), and it describes a fallback to 'a locally readable qualified copy', not an override of a pre-existing fail-closed decision with a content hash the bytes do not have.
findings.required_action: Before this step can be signed: (a) constrain the fallback to candidates whose own declared/document hash equals the requested one (or gate on byte equality, i.e. the design's segment 3), returning MISSING/unavailable otherwise; or (b) obtain explicit owner approval of S-10 recorded in the run directory, restated to cover this consequence (pre-B02 MISSING becomes REUSED_EXACT of a copy that fails both the size screen and the hash check). Add a regression case for this exact scenario to the F10 test file.

findings.claim: Implied claim: B02's qualification change inside service._annotate_locations is safe for existing consumers of is_canonical / duplicate_relation (nothing outside service.py + resolver.py changes behaviour).
findings.evidence: Temp harness probe_a2_single_root.py (single 'dayu' root, the documented production rejections layout ACME/filings/.rejections/123/2025.pdf + ACME/filings/.rejections/456/2025.pdf, identical bytes/sidecar). Locations after scan: both original_primary + active, same source_id, same document_id; duplicate_keys CTE returns two groups with n=2. PRE-B02  -> 'list_groups OK, total_groups = 2'. POST-B02 -> 'list_groups RAISED: StopIteration' at duplicate_cleanup.py:228 (`canonical = next(item for item in locations if item["is_canonical"])`, no default). Also reproduced with a two-root variant (companies/.rejections + Dropbox/.rejections). The consumer is user-reachable: cli.py:1151-1157 maps the 'duplicates' command onto DuplicateCleanupService(...).list_groups(...), and cli.py:1551-1559 turns the exception into a structured error + exit code 1.
findings.impact: The whole 'duplicates' listing fails (not just the offending group) on catalogs that contain two rejected copies of the same document - a layout the scanner itself produces (scanner.py:619 sets source_status=upstream_rejected but scanner.py:1115-1118 still writes location_status='active' when a source_id exists; adapters/dayu.py:94-97 documents the ticker/filings/.rejections/<id> group key). Operators lose the ability to list/recycle ANY duplicate group. Root cause is B02: pre-B02 every non-empty (document_id, source_id) group always produced an is_canonical=True row; B02 makes canonical status conditional on the new qualification while the unmodified consumer still assumes the old invariant. No test covers this and the evidence documents do not mention it.
findings.required_action: Restore an explicit invariant for the (document_id, source_id) group (e.g. always elect a canonical among the group's active original_primary rows, marking excluded ones separately) or make duplicate_cleanup.list_groups tolerant of a fully-excluded group. Because duplicate_cleanup.py is outside the B02 allowed set (F1/F2/F10), the in-scope fix is inside service.py; if a consumer change is judged necessary, stop and register the scope question per task_plan.md section 3. Add a regression case with two rejected copies of one document.

findings.claim: Evidence section 6 ('side effects'): the only counting change is that exact_duplicate_location_count / exact_original_copy_count now count qualified copies; 'the write face, outbound face and worker face are untouched apart from _duplicate_summary'.
findings.evidence: Temp harness probe_scenarios.py mixed (companies/.../.rejections/2025.pdf with best priority p10 + Dropbox copy p30 + future_lake copy p40, identical bytes), same code both trees: PRE-B02  -> list_groups: total_reclaimable_copies = 3, reclaimable_paths = ['2025.pdf', '2025.pdf', '2025.pdf.source.json']. POST-B02 -> total_reclaimable_copies = 2, reclaimable_paths = ['2025.pdf', '2025.pdf.source.json'] (the .rejections copy is no longer offered for recycling). Cause: excluded rows now get duplicate_relation='' (service.py:691-707), which duplicate_cleanup._public_location/eligibility reads.
findings.impact: Provider-rejected copies - precisely the files an operator wants to reclaim - silently disappear from the duplicate-cleanup planner; the same change of is_canonical also alters the exported index rows (service.py:996-1014 exports is_canonical/canonical_location_id/duplicate counts), so the 'outbound face is untouched' statement is imprecise. Neither effect is covered by a test.
findings.required_action: Decide and document whether rejected copies stay reclaimable/exported; if they should, do not route eligibility through the new exclusion flag. Update evidence section 6 to state the export/cleanup consequences of the re-based is_canonical/duplicate_relation.

findings.claim: Design B02 read-budget rule 3: 'any candidate-count or byte ceiling exceeded -> blocked (reason=budget_exceeded), with the undecided candidates listed in diagnostics'. Resolver comment (resolver.py:144-151): an over-budget/unverifiable candidate 'is simply NOT reusable ... the request keeps its existing MISSING/placeholder semantics - it never silently reuses bytes that were not verified'.
findings.evidence: Temp harness probe_scenarios.py budget_reuse, SourceResolver(catalog, read_budget=_ReadBudget(max_candidates=1)). 1st resolve: reused_exact, counters candidates=1 bytes_read=28 (verified, trace ['2025: matched']). 2nd resolve on the SAME resolver: reused_exact, download_required=false, trace ['2025: unverified_bytes', '2025: candidate <loc>:budget_exceeded', '2025: matched'], counters unchanged (candidates=1, bytes_read=28). 3rd resolve with a NEW resolver but the SAME budget object: identical unverified_bytes result. Also: test_r4b02_budget_counters_bound_candidate_reads pins REUSED_EXACT + unverified_bytes when the byte ceiling is exceeded.
findings.impact: Two real deviations from the design: (1) budget exhaustion returns a REUSED_EXACT handle instead of the design's blocked/unavailable, and (2) _ReadBudget carries state across requests, so any caller that reuses a budget (or a resolver) silently loses ALL verification for every later request while still receiving reuse handles. No production caller injects read_budget today (grep: only tests), so the exposure is currently limited to the new public parameter, but the failure mode is silent and the module comment quoted above contradicts the code.
findings.required_action: Make a reused budget fail loudly (or reset it per resolve()), and either implement blocked-on-exceed or register it as its own named deviation (it is currently only folded into S-10 'by extension' in evidence section 3/4). Correct the resolver.py:144-151 comment so it describes the fallback.

findings.claim: Claim: '_handle now returns _Selection (handle + reason + tried) and resolve records the reason in debug_trace whenever the served copy is NOT the preferred one'; comment in _annotate_locations: 'a document carrying two source revisions has one rank-1 row per revision'.
findings.evidence: Temp harness probe_scenarios.py twogroups: fabricated second source_id for the same document (sources.content_sha256 is UNIQUE, store.py DDL, so this needed a different hash + SQL surgery), the foreign group's rank-1 tried first (location_id tie-break) and its bytes mutated. Result: served from the document's own group with trace ['entity_gate_rejected: 0', '2025: matched'] only - the failed foreign rank-1 never appears, because the reason string is 'verified_candidate_rank_1' (identical to the ordinary preferred-copy case) and resolve only emits 'tried' when the reason differs. Integrity itself is fine: the served copy's bytes did match document.content_sha256.
findings.impact: The diagnostics guarantee is not total (rank-only reasons are ambiguous across groups, 'tried' can be dropped), and the state it protects against is unreachable in a well-formed catalog: source_id and document_id are both derived from the content hash (source_manifest.source_id_for_sha256, scanner._document_id_for_source) and sources.content_sha256 is UNIQUE, so one document cannot hold two source groups. The comment therefore describes an impossible state as if it were supported.
findings.required_action: Emit 'tried' whenever it is non-empty regardless of reason, make the reason identify the group (e.g. include the source_id suffix), and correct/qualify the two-revision comment and the matching docstring in the new test file.

findings.claim: Evidence claims (b02-implementation.md section 7 / b02-verification.json): '7/7 executed checks pass', coverage gate '2 passed' with resolver.py 87.36% and service.py 95.16%, and the record is re-runnable from the artifact.
findings.evidence: Numbers themselves reproduce EXACTLY on my own full re-run: 'python -m pytest tests/ -q --tb=line --cov=src/company_wiki/source_catalog --cov-branch --cov-report=json:<temp>' -> 2684 passed, 7 skipped, 420 warnings in 898.72s; from my coverage.json: resolver.py 87.36% (607/675 lines, 222/274 branches), service.py 95.16% (362/372, 110/124) - identical to the claim; re-evaluating the FC-1204 tables against my measurement: TIER1/TIER2+FROZEN failures = NONE. BUT the recorded artifact is bound to a pre-commit tree: b02-verification.json says "wiki_head": "c986c7a" (parent, not cab1fd6) and quotes a coverage.json whose meta.timestamp is 2026-09-12T12:27:31 - that file is NOT what the repo tracks. The tracked coverage.json (committed in 90fb08d, meta.timestamp 2026-08-17T20:58:29) yields resolver 85.64 / service 94.42, and the documented command run now gives: 'FC1204_COVERAGE_GATE=1 python -m pytest -q tests/contract/test_fc1204_coverage_ratchet.py' -> 2 failed ('service.py branch coverage 94.4% < 95% (required)', plus evidence_query.py 49.1% < 87%, extraction_quality.py 74.3% < 77%, security_identity.py 73.5% < 77%).
findings.impact: A reviewer or CI step that runs the recorded ratchet command against the committed tree sees red for a reason unrelated to B02 (stale tracked coverage.json), and the headline coverage evidence cannot be re-checked from the committed state without a 15-minute suite re-run. The check itself is honest - it just is not self-contained.
findings.required_action: Record the post-commit HEAD in b02-verification.json, state explicitly that the coverage gate requires the immediately preceding --cov run (and that the tracked coverage.json is stale), and keep the raw coverage artifact (or its file-level numbers) with the evidence.

findings.claim: Segment-2/segment-3 qualification rules: 'a .rejections path is never reusable' and 'a candidate whose bytes are not local (cloud placeholder) is refused without reading it / the query path performs no network I/O'.
findings.evidence: Direct calls to service._location_exclusion_reason in a temp probe: healthy -> '', role='original_attachment' -> 'role_not_original_primary', status='retired' -> 'location_status_retired', source_id='' -> 'source_id_missing', r'ACME\raw\.rejections\2025.pdf' -> 'rejections_path' - all four reasons correct. However the same probe returns 'rejections_path' for 'annual/my.rejections_backup/2025.pdf', because the test is a substring match on the normalised relative path (service.py:55-57); pre-B02 that same substring test existed only inside resolver._handle, so its blast radius is now the canonical election, duplicate counts, the exported index and the cleanup planner. Separately, _needs_hydration (resolver.py:157) tests only FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS|OFFLINE (0x400000|0x1000); FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_OPEN (0x40000) and cloud reparse tags are not covered, and the no-network evidence (test_r4b02_cloud_placeholder_candidate_is_not_read) is a monkeypatched Path.stat - no real placeholder exists in this environment to test against.
findings.impact: An unrelated path containing the substring '.rejections' is silently disqualified from canonical election and from duplicate accounting/cleanup; a RECALL_ON_OPEN placeholder would pass the probe and be opened (hydrated) inside resolve, which is what 'qualification must not use the network' forbids.
findings.required_action: Match .rejections as a path segment rather than a substring; widen the hydration attribute set (or record the cloud case as not_verified, consistent with the run's D0-only evidence layer).

defects_found: B-VR02-01: unverified - and provably non-matching - bytes are served as reused_exact with download_required=false where pre-B02 returned missing (fallback path in resolver._select_candidate); the equivalence wording of the claim and the L03 acceptance line ('all copies unusable -> unavailable, do not take another revision') do not hold, and S-10 is explicitly unapproved.

B-VR02-02: duplicate_cleanup.list_groups raises StopIteration (new regression from B02's is_canonical change) whenever a (document_id, source_id) duplicate group consists only of active .rejections rows - reproduced with the standard ticker/filings/.rejections/<id> layout; the whole 'duplicates' CLI command fails.

B-VR02-03: rejected copies silently drop out of the duplicate-cleanup reclaimable set (3 -> 2 in the mixed fixture); the exported index's is_canonical/canonical_location_id also change, so 'the outbound face is untouched' is imprecise.

B-VR02-04: budget exhaustion returns a reuse handle instead of the design's blocked, and a reused _ReadBudget silently degrades every later request to unverified bytes; the resolver.py:144-151 comment contradicts the code.

B-VR02-05: 'verified_candidate_rank_1' is ambiguous across source groups and suppresses the 'tried' diagnostics; the two-source-group state the code comments describe is forbidden by the schema (sources.content_sha256 UNIQUE + hash-derived ids).

B-VR02-06: b02-verification.json is bound to the pre-commit HEAD (c986c7a) and to a coverage.json that is not the tracked one; the recorded ratchet command currently fails on the committed tree (2 failed) even though the underlying numbers reproduce exactly.

B-VR02-07: '.rejections' is matched as a substring (confirmed false positive on 'annual/my.rejections_backup/2025.pdf') with an enlarged blast radius, and the placeholder mask omits FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_OPEN; the zero-network evidence is a monkeypatched stat.
